changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance buyers (CFO, controller) at mid-market B2B distributors, open with this line instead of our usual opener: "Know where your money is. Every deposit matched to its invoice automatically, so month-end stops being a week of archaeology."
changes.why: Reconciliation was the only message that landed, and it got the CFO to interrupt the demo, while her own words ('where my money is', 'a week of archaeology', 'the deposits') name the pain more sharply than 'payout reconciles'.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: "Send us one month of your statements and we'll cost your manual matching: your number, not ours." Offer this to finance buyers in place of the independent study, and use Wen's Tallowfield model as the template once it is recovered.
changes.why: The CFO asked to see it with her own data, the controller supplied the statements, and she accepted the result as 'my number, not yours', which is the opposite of a third-party study.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Don't open with global growth or currencies (or follow with M2's developer/API pitch) for regional B2B sellers with small IT teams that don't build; lead with the M9 replacement instead.
changes.why: The global/infrastructure opener and the developer pitch got silence from a three-state supplier whose four-person IT team builds nothing, and no one on the customer side ever said 'infrastructure'.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For buyers leaving a bank-bundled processor: "A named contact who knows your account, not a queue." Use this only once post-sale confirms who owns that commitment; the AE's 'me' is not a service promise.
changes.why: After the bank answered with a rate offer she hadn't asked for, the CFO's only new question was whether she'd get a named contact, because her bank rep had changed. That points to relationship decay, not tiered response times, as the switching opening.
